hypothesis: A rigorously engineered, windowed feature and labeling pipeline that merges quantum and classical telemetry and applies imbalance-handling strategies will (a) produce ML-ready train/validation/test datasets with no measurable label leakage, (b) achieve higher downstream baseline detection performance (e.g., ROC-AUC, PR-AUC) than a naive row-level telemetry export, and (c) remain reproducible across runs via explicit dataset versioning and deterministic configuration.

baseline.description: Naive per-record export of simulated quantum and classical telemetry from Chapter 6 without structured windows, engineered aggregates, or explicit imbalance handling.
baseline.data_source: Raw CSV/Parquet telemetry exported by the Chapter 6 simulator (e.g., `simulated_telemetry_raw.parquet`), containing timestamped quantum link metrics (QBER, key rate, loss, alarms) and basic classical network/device counters.
pipeline_steps: Load raw telemetry files for one or more simulation runs.
Drop rows with missing required fields via simple row-wise deletion.
Keep only a minimal subset of fields: timestamp, link_id, qber, key_rate, loss_db, classical_if_util, label_attack (boolean or categorical).
No windowing or aggregation; each telemetry row is treated as an independent sample.
Forward-fill labels for rows where label_attack is missing using last-observed label for the same link_id; rows with no label history are dropped.
No feature scaling, normalization, or encoding beyond simple numeric casting.
Naive random 70/15/15 split into train/validation/test across the entire table without grouping by simulation run, scenario, or time.
No explicit dataset versioning; export a single `baseline_dataset.parquet` file overwriting any existing file.
expected_characteristics: Samples are highly temporally correlated across splits, making label leakage likely.
Attack vs. non-attack class imbalance is unaddressed and reflects raw simulator prevalence.
No consistent event or window definition; downstream models must infer structure themselves.
Dataset reproducibility depends implicitly on simulator output ordering and random state but is not recorded as metadata.

treatment.description: Structured, configurable data pipeline that converts quantum and classical telemetry into windowed, aggregated, labeled records with explicit imbalance handling and dataset versioning.
treatment.data_source: Same raw telemetry files as baseline, plus scenario/attack metadata files produced by the Chapter 6 simulator (e.g., `runs/<run_id>/telemetry.parquet`, `runs/<run_id>/scenario_meta.json`).
pipeline_steps: Label construction with clear policies for uncertainty

1_config_driven_run_selection.goal: Ensure that the same subset of simulation runs and time ranges is used consistently across experiments and that configuration is captured as part of dataset metadata.
inputs: List of run_ids to include or glob pattern (e.g., `run_*`).
behavior: Iterate over runs under `data_root` and load `scenario_meta.json` for each.
Filter runs based on declared scenario, attack type, or other metadata fields.
Materialize an ordered list of `selected_runs` with full paths to telemetry and metadata files.

2_event_window_definition.goal: Transform fine-grained telemetry into ML samples via consistent time windows or event-centered windows suitable for detection tasks.

window_types.name: fixed_sliding_time_window
window_types.description: Fixed-duration windows sliding over time for each link/channel, used for continuous anomaly/attack detection.

parameters.alignment: left-aligned on earliest timestamp in window or floored to nearest stride boundary

window_types.name: event_centered_window
window_types.description: Windows centered around detected or injected attack onset events, combining pre- and post-onset telemetry.

parameters.event_source: attack_onset timestamps per run and link from `scenario_meta.json`

indexing.window_id_definition: Hash of (run_id, link_id, window_start, window_end) or an incremental integer per link_id and run_id.

3_feature_engineering.goal: Create robust, interpretable features for quantum metrics and classical telemetry within each window.
quantum_features: qber_trend_slope (via simple linear regression over time within window)
count_of_quantum_alarms (e.g., device or protocol alarms) within window
statistical_descriptors: skewness and kurtosis for qber and key_rate (for sufficiently sampled windows)
autocorrelation_lag1 for key_rate or qber (simple AR(1) proxy within window)

normalization.approach: Compute feature-wise mean and std over training set only; apply z-score standardization to train/val/test using training statistics. Persist statistics in metadata for reuse.
normalization.leakage_prevention: No normalization statistics calculated on validation or test splits.

4_quantum_classical_fusion.goal: Represent the combined state of quantum and classical planes for a link within each window as a single feature vector.
method: Inner-join quantum and classical telemetry on (run_id, link_id, timestamp) where appropriate; otherwise treat them as separate streams with unified windowing.
For each window, compute aggregations separately for quantum and classical features as defined above.
Concatenate features into a unified feature vector with prefixed names (e.g., `q_`, `c_` prefixes).
Ensure feature schemas are identical across runs via consistent column ordering and missing-value imputation (e.g., median imputation based on training data for numeric fields).

5_labeling_strategy.goal: Assign labels to each window for supervised or semi-supervised detection tasks, while handling ambiguous time periods explicitly.
label_sources: Per-timestamp attack flags from simulator output (if available).
Scenario-level metadata indicating attack presence, type, and approximate time interval per run and link.
Derived anomalies based on quantum metrics (e.g., QBER spike exceeding threshold over baseline) when no explicit attack ground truth exists.

label_policies.name: attack_window_labeling
label_policies.definition: A window is labeled `attack` (1) if the fraction of timestamps within it overlapped by a known attack is greater than or equal to a configurable threshold (e.g., 0.3).

label_policies.name: clean_window_labeling
label_policies.definition: A window is labeled `clean` (0) if it has zero overlap with any known attack interval and is not marked anomalous by derived anomaly rules.

label_policies.name: uncertain_window_handling
label_policies.definition: Windows with partial but below-threshold attack coverage or with conflicting indicators (e.g., suspicious QBER spike but no attack ground truth) are labeled `uncertain` and can be either dropped or reserved for semi-supervised use.

multiclass_labels.derivation: Map from scenario_meta attack_type and failure_type fields to categorical labels; non-attack failure modes get dedicated labels where distinguishable.

label_consistency_checks: Verify that attack windows cover the attack intervals reported in scenario metadata within a tolerance (e.g., ±1 window stride).
Ensure no windows overlapping known attacks are labeled `clean` unless deliberately excluded as `uncertain`.

6_imbalance_handling.goal: Address scarcity of attack windows relative to clean windows while keeping evaluation realistic and avoiding leakage.

techniques.name: class_weights
techniques.description: Compute class weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the training split only; store in dataset metadata for downstream models.

techniques.name: attack_oversampling
techniques.description: Optionally oversample minority attack windows in the training set via simple random oversampling or SMOTE-like algorithms applied to features only (no test/validation oversampling).

techniques.name: time_blocking_for_eval
techniques.description: Evaluation splits remain naturally imbalanced to reflect realistic prevalence; imbalance handling is not applied to validation/test splits.

7_data_quality_and_leakage_checks.goal: Automatically detect common data issues before exporting final datasets.
checks: Missing values per feature, reported as counts and fractions per split.
Constant or near-constant features that may be dropped.
Feature-target correlations that appear suspiciously high due to leakage (e.g., explicit attack flags included as features).
Temporal overlap across splits when grouping by run_id or time (e.g., ensuring runs or time blocks assigned to train are not reused in validation/test).
Label distribution per split (class counts and proportions).
leakage_prevention: Exclude direct attack flags or obviously post-hoc indicators (e.g., `attack_detected`, `incident_id`) from feature set.
Ensure that normalization and imbalance parameters are derived solely from training data.
Ensure group-based splitting by run_id or link_id when required by experimental design.

8_deterministic_splitting_and_versioning.goal: Provide reproducible data splits and traceable dataset versions tied to configuration and raw inputs.

splitting_strategies.name: run_based_split
splitting_strategies.description: Partition full runs into train/validation/test sets so that telemetry from a single run_id never appears in more than one split.

splitting_strategies.name: time_based_split_within_run
splitting_strategies.description: Within each run_id, partition windows into train/validation/test based on time, preserving order (e.g., first 60% of time for training, next 20% validation, last 20% test).
splitting_strategies.conditions: Used when there are few distinct runs but long time series per run.

determinism.shuffling: If any operation requires shuffling (e.g., oversampling or random split selection among runs), it must use the fixed random_seed.

versioning.metadata_file: JSON file saved as `datasets/<dataset_id>/metadata.json` capturing configuration, raw input hashes, feature schema, and splitting strategy.

workloads.name: W1_5s_sliding_windows_binary_attack_detection
workloads.description: Transform raw telemetry into 5-second sliding windows for each link, label windows as attack vs. clean, and export balanced train/validation/test splits with preserved temporal order.
workloads.baseline_variant: Apply the same selection of runs but skip windowing/aggregation and instead treat individual telemetry records as samples, then produce naive random 70/15/15 splits.

workloads.name: W2_event_centered_eavesdropping_vs_clean
workloads.description: Construct event-centered windows around eavesdropping attacks and compare them to benign windows of equivalent size for a targeted binary classification task.
workloads.baseline_variant: Use all telemetry rows occurring within the [pre_event, post_event] intervals as attack samples and a random subset of benign rows as clean samples; no windowing or feature aggregation.

workloads.name: W3_multiclass_attack_type_classification
workloads.description: Generate windowed datasets labeled by attack type (eavesdrop, jamming, misconfiguration) vs. clean, for multiclass supervised learning.
workloads.baseline_variant: Use single telemetry rows sampled at fixed intervals (e.g., every second) with instantaneous labels, no aggregation or temporal features.

comparability: Use identical raw input runs for baseline and treatment by applying the same run selection logic.
Where possible, ensure that downstream ML models used to evaluate quality are identical in architecture and hyperparameters across baseline and treatment.
Use the same random_seed (42) for any stochastic operation in both pipelines.

Ensure that train/validation/test splits for baseline and treatment are comparable by run_id membership (e.g., if a run_id is in the training set for the treatment, all its rows are also in the training set for the baseline).
data_integrity: Verify that record counts and time ranges per run_id are preserved across baseline and treatment prior to transformation (no unintentional row loss).
Validate that quantum metrics distributions in raw data match between baseline and treatment inputs.
implementation: Implement both baseline and treatment pipelines in Python using the same versions of pandas, NumPy, and supporting libraries.
Run both pipelines on the same hardware or environment profile to ensure comparable performance measurements where collected.

metrics.name: num_samples_train
metrics.description: Number of training samples (windows or raw rows) in the exported training set.

metrics.name: class_distribution_train
metrics.description: Distribution of labels in the training set, reported as a mapping from class to (count, proportion).

metrics.name: class_distribution_val
metrics.description: Label distribution in the validation set.

metrics.name: class_distribution_test
metrics.description: Label distribution in the test set.

metrics.name: num_features
metrics.description: Number of feature columns in the final dataset (excluding ID and label columns).

metrics.name: missing_value_rate_per_feature
metrics.description: For each feature, the fraction of samples with missing values, per split.

metrics.name: temporal_leakage_indicator
metrics.description: Indicator or fraction of run_ids/time blocks that appear in more than one split (should be zero in treatment).

metrics.name: split_reproducibility
metrics.description: Whether rerunning the pipeline with the same configuration and seed yields identical checksums for exported split files.

metrics.name: feature_target_correlation_max
metrics.description: Maximum absolute Pearson correlation between any single feature and the label in the training set, used as a heuristic to spot potential leakage.

metrics.name: dataset_build_time
metrics.description: Wall-clock time to execute the pipeline and produce all splits and metadata, per workload.

metrics.name: downstream_baseline_roc_auc
metrics.description: ROC-AUC of a fixed simple ML baseline model (e.g., RandomForestClassifier) trained on the produced training data and evaluated on the test set. Used as a proxy for dataset utility.
metrics.note: This metric is optional and measured when integrating with Chapter 8 experiments.

metrics.name: downstream_baseline_pr_auc
metrics.description: Precision-Recall AUC for the same baseline model as above on the test set.

data_quality_and_leakage: For treatment datasets, `temporal_leakage_indicator` must be false (no run_ids or time blocks shared across train/validation/test splits).
For treatment datasets, `missing_value_rate_per_feature` must be below a configurable threshold (e.g., < 5%) for all core features, or affected features must be clearly documented and imputed.
Direct ground-truth flags (e.g., `attack_flag`, `attack_type_raw`) must not appear in the feature set; if present in raw data, they are removed or reserved only for labels.
`split_reproducibility` must evaluate to true: repeated runs with identical configuration produce identical checksums/hashes of the dataset files.
class_balance_and_labeling: For workloads using class weighting, computed class weights must be finite and positive for all classes present in the training set.
In binary tasks, the minority class (attack) must constitute at least a minimal presence in the training set (e.g., > 1% of samples), achieved via oversampling or scenario selection as needed.
No windows overlapping known attack intervals should be labeled `clean` unless explicitly categorized as `uncertain` and excluded from main splits.
comparative_performance: Treatment-based datasets must not degrade downstream baseline ROC-AUC and PR-AUC relative to the baseline dataset for the same ML model and raw inputs. A non-negative difference is considered acceptable, with a targeted improvement of at least +0.02 in ROC-AUC where feasible.
Number of features in the treatment dataset must be reasonable for the audience’s operational constraints (e.g., <= 200 features) while maintaining or improving downstream performance.
operational_reproducibility: All configuration required to rebuild a dataset (window parameters, labels, imbalance strategy, splitting strategy, seeds, and version tags) must be captured in `metadata.json` under the dataset directory.
The pipeline must support reruns on new raw simulation outputs by changing only configuration values, not core code.

failure_modes.name: label_leakage_via_future_information
failure_modes.description: Features in a window inadvertently depend on telemetry from timestamps after the window end (e.g., including post-attack recovery information for pre-attack windows), enabling unrealistically high model performance.
failure_modes.detection: Temporal leakage checks comparing window time ranges against underlying attack intervals and verifying that only data within [window_start, window_end] is used.
failure_modes.mitigation: Restrict all feature computations to lie strictly within window boundaries and remove any feature derived from future timestamps.

failure_modes.name: feature_includes_ground_truth
failure_modes.description: Attack flags or scenario IDs inadvertently included as features rather than only as labels or grouping identifiers.
failure_modes.detection: Automatic scanning of feature names for substrings like `attack`, `label`, `scenario`; computation of feature-target correlations to identify near-perfect correlation.
failure_modes.mitigation: Maintain an explicit allowlist of feature names and strip any fields identified as ground truth from the feature matrix; rerun pipeline.

failure_modes.name: misaligned_windows_across_streams
failure_modes.description: Quantum and classical telemetry are windowed differently, resulting in inconsistent or misaligned samples when fused, which can distort relationships.
failure_modes.detection: Check that for each window_id, the quantum and classical aggregations use identical window_start and window_end boundaries and that sample counts per stream are reasonable.
failure_modes.mitigation: Centralize window boundary generation and ensure both streams are aggregated against the same index.

failure_modes.name: severe_class_imbalance_unaddressed
failure_modes.description: Attack windows are too rare in the training set, causing downstream models to default to predicting only the majority class.
failure_modes.detection: Inspect `class_distribution_train` and verify that the minority class proportion falls below a configured threshold (e.g., < 1%).
failure_modes.mitigation: Enable oversampling, adjust scenario selection to include more attack runs, or design semi-supervised experiments for anomaly detection instead of supervised attack classification.

failure_modes.name: non_reproducible_splits
failure_modes.description: Train/validation/test splits differ across runs due to changing seeds or uncontrolled sources of randomness.
failure_modes.detection: Compare file checksums or sample indices across two independent runs with the same configuration; differences indicate non-determinism.
failure_modes.mitigation: Audit all uses of randomization in the pipeline and ensure they are seeded via a single configuration parameter; avoid operations with non-deterministic parallelism where possible.

failure_modes.name: skewed_feature_statistics_due_to_including_val_test
failure_modes.description: Normalization statistics accidentally computed on the full dataset, leaking validation/test information into training preprocessing.
failure_modes.detection: Verify that the set of samples used to compute statistics matches the training set only, by logging and cross-checking sample IDs.
failure_modes.mitigation: Perform splitting before normalization, and centralize statistic computation in a component that explicitly consumes only training data.

failure_modes.name: overly_complex_feature_space
failure_modes.description: Excessive number of features relative to the sample count, increasing risk of overfitting and impairing interpretability.
failure_modes.detection: Monitor `num_features` and apply simple heuristics, e.g., `num_samples_train / num_features` below a certain ratio.
failure_modes.mitigation: Introduce feature selection or dimensionality reduction, or simplify feature sets for some workloads; clearly document any reduced feature variants.

hardware.storage: At least 20 GB of free disk space for raw simulation outputs and multiple dataset versions.
hardware.gpu: Not required for dataset preparation; optional for downstream ML experiments.

relevant_paths: data/sim_runs/  # Default location for raw telemetry and metadata outputs
configs/ch7/  # YAML/JSON configuration files for workloads
datasets/  # Output directory for ML-ready datasets

run_instructions: 1. Clone the repository: `git clone https://github.com/bookauthority/ai-quantum-threat-detection-guide.git` and `cd ai-quantum-threat-detection-guide`.
2. Create and activate a Python 3.10 virtual environment (e.g., using `python3.10 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate` on Unix-like systems).
3. Install required Python packages: `pip install -r requirements-ch7.txt` (where `requirements-ch7.txt` pins versions listed in the required_environment).

4. Ensure that the Chapter 6 simulator has been executed and that raw telemetry is available under `data/sim_runs/`. If not, follow Chapter 6 instructions (e.g., run `python simulator/run_simulations.py --output-root data/sim_runs --num-runs 20 --scenarios all`).
5. Inspect or create configuration files for the desired workloads under `configs/ch7/`. Example files:
- `configs/ch7/w1_5s_sliding_binary.yaml` for W1.
- `configs/ch7/w2_event_centered_eavesdrop.yaml` for W2.
- `configs/ch7/w3_multiclass_attack_types.yaml` for W3.
6. To generate the baseline (naive) dataset for a workload, run the baseline script. Example for W1:
- `python pipelines/ch7_dataset_build/build_baseline_dataset.py --config configs/ch7/w1_5s_sliding_binary.yaml --output-root datasets/ --random-seed 42`.
This script will:
- Load raw telemetry from `data/sim_runs/` according to the config.
- Apply the naive row-level pipeline.
- Produce a baseline dataset directory, e.g., `datasets/ch7-w1-baseline/`, containing `train.parquet`, `val.parquet`, `test.parquet`, and `metadata.json`.
7. To generate the treatment (engineered) dataset for the same workload, run:
- `python pipelines/ch7_dataset_build/build_dataset.py --config configs/ch7/w1_5s_sliding_binary.yaml --output-root datasets/ --dataset-id ch7-w1-qc-fused-5s-win --random-seed 42`.
This script will:
- Load the same raw telemetry and scenario metadata as the baseline run.
- Apply windowing, feature engineering, labeling, imbalance handling, and splitting as specified.
- Export ML-ready datasets under `datasets/ch7-w1-qc-fused-5s-win/` (or another dataset_id if specified).

8. Verify reproducibility by rerunning the treatment command with the same parameters and confirming that file checksums or hashes (e.g., via `sha256sum datasets/ch7-w1-qc-fused-5s-win/*.parquet`) remain unchanged.
9. (Optional) Run built-in quality and leakage checks by executing:
- `python pipelines/ch7_dataset_build/validate_dataset.py --dataset-root datasets/ch7-w1-qc-fused-5s-win/`.

This will compute and print metrics such as missing_value_rate_per_feature, class distributions, temporal_leakage_indicator, and feature_target_correlation_max, storing results consistent with the evidence_schema.
10. Repeat steps 6–9 for W2 and W3 by substituting the appropriate configuration files and dataset_id values.
11. (Optional, for end-to-end verification with Chapter 8) Train a simple baseline model on both baseline and treatment datasets and record ROC-AUC and PR-AUC to empirically compare dataset utility.
12. Archive or commit dataset metadata files (`metadata.json`, `feature_stats.json`, `class_weights.json`) alongside experiment notes to ensure traceability.

evidence_schema.description: Schema for storing objective evidence and measurements from running the dataset construction experiments. No outcomes are pre-filled here; this defines the structure that actual experiment runs should populate.

experiment_id.description: Identifier of the experiment configuration used, e.g., `exp-ch7-quantum-telemetry-to-ml-ready-datasets-v1`.

timestamp_utc.description: UTC timestamp when the experiment run completed.

package_versions.description: Mapping from package name to installed version (e.g., pandas, numpy, scikit-learn).

variant.description: Indicates whether the recorded evidence is for the baseline or treatment pipeline.

config_path.description: Path to the configuration file used for this run.

dataset_id.description: Identifier of the produced dataset, typically matching the dataset directory name.

missing_value_rate_per_feature.description: For each feature name, missing value rates per split.

leakage_fraction.description: Fraction of run_ids or time blocks that appear in multiple splits.

downstream_baseline_roc_auc.description: If measured by training a standard baseline model using this dataset.

downstream_baseline_pr_auc.description: If measured by training a standard baseline model using this dataset.

checksums.description: SHA-256 checksums for key output files, used to verify reproducibility.

notes.description: Free-text field for any qualitative observations, anomalies, or deviations from the planned protocol.
